chunk.title: Guide: reading health signals
chunk.heading: Error rate
chunk.text:
The share of requests that fail, usually counted as HTTP 5xx responses. It is the
clearest sign that users are affected. Find the onset: the first point where the rate
rises above its normal level. The onset is the moment you compare with recent changes.

provenance.kind: synthetic runbook authored for RECAP V1

chunk.title: ShopSim architecture
chunk.heading: Service level objectives
chunk.text:
- Errors: the HTTP 5xx ratio of every service stays under 1% of requests.
- Latency: p95 latency stays under 500 ms for every service.
- Availability: all replicas of every service report ready.

An alert fires when a service breaks one of these objectives. The alert names the
service whose numbers crossed the line, which is not always the service that is broken.

provenance.kind: synthetic runbook authored for RECAP V1

chunk.title: ShopSim architecture
chunk.heading: Call graph
chunk.text:
- frontend calls checkout and cart.
- checkout calls payment and inventory.
- payment, inventory and cart call no other service.

A service that another service calls is its dependency; the service making the call is
the caller. Requests therefore flow from frontend to checkout, and from checkout to
payment and inventory.

chunk.title: Runbook: memory pressure and crash loops
chunk.heading: Symptoms
chunk.text:
- `OOMKilled` events: a container exceeded its memory limit and was killed.
- `BackOff` events and a `CrashLoopBackOff` status while the pod keeps restarting.
- Readiness probe failures, so fewer replicas are ready than desired.
- The memory metric climbs toward the limit; logs show heap warnings and
  `OutOfMemoryError` lines.
- The error rate rises because the remaining replicas take all the traffic.

chunk.title: Runbook: bad deployment
chunk.heading: Remediation
chunk.text:
Mechanism: bad_deployment
Recommended action: execute_rollback

Use the propose_rollback dry run first. It reports the current version and the last
healthy revision a rollback would restore, without changing anything. Roll back to that
revision only after a human approves the exact action: this incident, this service and
this target version.

provenance.kind: synthetic runbook authored for RECAP V1

chunk.title: Runbook: memory pressure and crash loops
chunk.heading: Remediation
chunk.text:
Mechanism: resource_pressure
Recommended action: restart_service

A rolling restart replaces pods one at a time, so the service keeps serving traffic. It
is reversible and safe when the service has at least two replicas, and it still needs an
approval bound to the exact service and incident. A restart does NOT fix a bad release:
the new pods run the same broken code and fail again.

proposals.rationale: The verified root cause is a bad deployment of the backend service, specifically version v1.1.0, which introduced errors causing HTTP 500 responses. The evidence shows that the error rate spiked shortly after the deployment, and the logs confirm a KeyError in the backend service. The recommended action for a bad deployment is to roll back to a previous version. The rollback should be executed to the last healthy revision, which is v1.0.0.
proposals.expected_health_change: The error rate should decrease as the backend service reverts to the previous version, which is known to be stable. The frontend service should also see a reduction in errors as the backend issue is resolved.
proposals.rollback_hint: The rollback will revert the backend service to version v1.0.0, which is the previous stable version. This should resolve the HTTP 500 errors and restore normal operation.
